payload.title: Markus: standard, config-driven analytics capability for static publications
payload.description:
Ryan 2026-10-03: analytics needs a simple standard way, and Markus needs to be aware of it. Today each publication would have to hand-roll a snippet (the Anth.us port omitted analytics entirely; live anth.us has it).

Goal: a publication-neutral analytics option on the Markus static renderer (e.g. SiteChrome.analytics or a build_markus_site argument) taking a small typed config, e.g. provider (start with Google Analytics 4 / gtag, the provider live anth.us uses; design so Plausible or others slot in), measurement id, an optional consent/opt-out mode, and enabled. The renderer emits the correct snippet in <head> on every page it renders, including pages rendered via render_page directly. Disabled or None (the default) emits nothing, so existing publications are BYTE-IDENTICAL (Pilobol.us proof required: 89 files, empty diff -r). No secrets in output beyond the public measurement id. Respect the security posture (no author-controlled script injection; the config comes from publication build code only). Docs in docs/ (where the Markus renderer is documented) plus tests. The Anth.us build will enable it only for production builds (PPY-f1f0a8 provides the analytics_enabled switch).
